subject: Mutual action plan & procurement sequencing for Curelytics evaluation
messages:

To: maya.rao@curelytics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-10-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP + evaluation plan + next steps

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, I’m attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a linked evaluation plan spreadsheet so we can align on success criteria and timing. High-level asks:

- Can Curelytics confirm the internal stakeholders who need to sign off on pilot acceptance (security, procurement, legal, product)?
- Are there any non-negotiable procurement gating items (e.g., SOC2, DPA language, regional data residency) we should account for up front?
- Proposed milestone cadence: design & environment prep (2w) -> pilot run (3w) -> acceptance + order form signature (1w).

Attachments: MAP-draft-Curelytics-v1.pdf, eval-plan-spreadsheet.xlsx

If that timeline looks broadly right I’ll draft a sequencing recommendation (MSA -> DPA -> Order Form) and identify where legal handoffs should happen. Happy to get a short sync on Thursday to walk the MAP.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: maya.rao@curelytics.com

Date: 2025-10-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + evaluation plan + next steps

Jonas —

Appreciate the materials. I shared with our head of procurement and legal; copying procurement. For stakeholders:

- Tom Henderson (legal) — will lead contract review
- Priya Singh (security) — will validate SOC2 and data flows
- Raj Patel (product) — pilot success criteria owner

Procurement notes: Curelytics needs SOC2 Type II report and a standard DPA; we prefer the MSA to be a relatively lightweight master agreement with most data/privacy specifics in the DPA.

Timelines: Your proposed cadence is reasonable but we typically build in an extra week for legal redlines if there’s any custom language.

Tom will send a redline matrix after he reviews the MSA — can you share the latest MSA text and a short data flow diagram? Also happy to do a 30m call next Tue (10/28) to sync.

—Maya
Maya Rao
Head of Partnerships
Curelytics

From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: maya.rao@curelytics.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-10-27T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + evaluation plan + next steps

Maya —

Thanks for the clarity and the stakeholder list. Per your ask I’ve attached a concise sequencing diagram (timeline-v1.png) and a proposed orchestration:

1) Internal prep & environment provisioning (Redwood & Curelytics infra alignment) — target 10/27–11/03
2) Contract baseline: exchange MSA (baseline) + draft DPA (we’ll propose Redwood’s standard DPA) — start 10/27
3) Pilot execution (3 weeks) — start ~11/04
4) Acceptance review, capture evaluation logs and metrics, and finalize Order Form (pricing + committed throughput) — target week of 11/24

Sequencing rationale:
- We suggest completing data/privacy taps (DPA, SOC2 evidence) before the pilot start to avoid rework in the pilot acceptance window.
- MSA should be accepted as a commercial framework early; detailed redlines can be handled in parallel with DPA.

Laura — can you take lead on procurement coordination (contract owner) and keep Karthik in the loop for any clauses that touch licensing/pricing?

I’ll upload a short MSA baseline to the shared Drive before our call Tuesday.

Jonas
From: thenderson@curelytics.com
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: maya.rao@curelytics.com
Date: 2025-10-29T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + evaluation plan + next steps

Jonas / team —

I reviewed the MAP and the MSA baseline you referenced on Drive. I’ve attached an initial redline (MSA_redlines_v2.docx) and a short matrix highlighting three items we consider gating:

1) Data processing definitions (clarify subprocessors and cross-border transfers)
2) Incident notification windows (we require 24h initial notice)
3) Indemnity carve-outs for regulated-data claims

We’ll need SOC2 Type II report for the prior 12 months (or an AICPA bridge letter) and a technical diagram that shows where customer PII lives and how KV cache is handled during the pilot. If Redwood can provide a DPA draft that maps to those items, it will speed our review.

I’ll come prepared to the 10/28 call with a redline summary and will prioritize turnaround so the pilot can start in early November.

Tom Henderson
Senior Counsel, Curelytics
